headline: Top Pentagon officials reportedly plan to keep an internal report on a US strike that killed more than 150 people at an Iranian school secret until after the November midterm elections.
score_reason: Anonymous-source report, but from Bloomberg with on-record reaction from a senator and the Pentagon; strong public-interest and AI-accountability angle.
importance_line: It affects victims' families and public oversight of how the military uses AI, since an earlier Bloomberg investigation reportedly found over-reliance on AI contributed to the strike, but the plan rests on anonymous sources and no final timeline is set.
summary: Bloomberg reports, as carried by The Straits Times, that advisers to Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth have told some Pentagon staff the report on the Minab school attack will wait until after the US midterms at the earliest, according to unnamed sources, though no final decision has been made. A Pentagon official said the investigation is ongoing, while Senator Kirsten Gillibrand, a New York Democrat on the Senate armed services panel, called the delay "disgraceful".
notes: Read on The Straits Times, which carries Bloomberg's text; credited to Bloomberg.
